Collapse reference rows the matcher cannot tell apart

Source: R/match.R
pf_collapse_reference.Rd

Rows sharing a normalized name, state and ZIP5 are indistinguishable to every comparison the cascade makes. Keeping 6,710 of them buys nothing and costs the blocking pass 6,710 candidates for every query that hits the name.

Usage

pf_collapse_reference(
  ref,
  by = c("name_key", "state", "zip5"),
  rebuild = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

ref

A bundle from pf_build_reference() or a normalized reference.

by

Columns defining indistinguishability. The default is the set the cascade actually compares on.

rebuild

Recompute name_freq, token_idf and ref_index from the collapsed reference. Leaving this FALSE keeps the pre-collapse name frequencies, which is a different system: np_name_freq() feeds the promotion gate, so a rebuild makes rare-after-collapse names newly eligible.

verbose

Report what was collapsed.

Value

The bundle with reference collapsed, plus members — one row per merged EIN, carrying rep_ein, ein and n_identical — and collapse, the summary statistics.

Measured, and NOT adopted

dev/PHASE3-LIBRARIES.md §0 listed this as one of two changes to make before the full run, on the strength of "reference −7%, cost driver −8x". Both halves reproduce on the right artifact and the blocker's own name_key (dev/probe-ref-collapse.R): 3,880,428 → 3,527,239 rows, 9.1% smaller, and sum(block^2) 4.49e8 → 5.66e7 — 7.9x. The largest (name, state) block falls from 7,379 rows to 1,208.

It buys nothing. Same rung, same queries, augmented against collapsed (dev/SHARD-RSS-COLLAPSED.log): peak working set 36.82 → 32.95 GB (−10.5%, still one shard on 68 GB) and 366 s per 1,000 either way — no speedup at all. A 7.9x cut in the cost driver moved the cost 0%.

The proxy is what failed. sum(block^2) counts candidates on the assumption that queries distribute like the reference. Grant recipients do not: nobody makes grants to 6,710 PEO chapters, so the giant blocks are almost never queried and shrinking them saves work nobody was doing.

What it hides

152,825 groups hold more than one EIN, covering 506,014 — 13.0% of the reference. Before the collapse that ambiguity was visible: tied candidates drove the margin to zero and np_tier() held the grant in MAYBE. Afterwards one row wins outright. On the 2,000-identity rung the collapse moved 80 grants MAYBE → YES, and 88% of them are won by an EIN standing for more than one — median 2, max 5,363. That is a 5% headline YES gain made entirely of converted abstentions, and it is why this function returns members rather than quietly dropping the merged EINs.

So: do not use this in the production cascade. It is kept because the negative result rests on it and because members is a usable same-name-same-place equivalence table in its own right — which is the reference-side duplicate problem of dev/CLUSTER-FINDINGS.md §8, and a better use for it than blocking.
